text: Deflationists claim that the truth predicate is essentially ___: asserting that 'snow is white' is true says no more than asserting that snow is white, ascending from the sentence to its use and back.
explanation: Quine's slogan is that 'disquotation is the whole of the concept': the truth predicate serves for semantic ascent and descent and for blind endorsement ('everything Newton said is true'), not to ascribe a substantive property. This is the core commitment of disquotational deflationism.
